symptoms: The job failed after a runtime upgrade and not after a code change
The message names a legacy configuration and tells the reader to set it
The same code against the same data succeeded on the previous runtime
likely_causes: The upgraded Spark changed a default, and the value the data was written with is no longer the value the read assumes
Datetime values written by an older writer are being read under a calendar the new runtime resolves differently
The job carries a legacy configuration that the new runtime removed or renamed
diagnostic_steps: Read which legacy configuration the message names -- this exception is unusual in that it tells the reader what to set, and the name is the diagnosis
Read the legacy configuration the job already declares: a job that carries one the new runtime removed fails for a different reason than one that carries none
Confirm the runtime versions on both sides of the upgrade, because the exception says a behaviour changed and not which change
fixes: Set the configuration the message names, when preserving the previous behaviour is the intent
Rewrite the affected data under the new behaviour, when moving forward is the intent -- and this is a data change, not a configuration one
Replace a removed legacy configuration with the property that succeeded it
unsafe_fixes: Setting the legacy configuration and moving on without recording it: the flag preserves old behaviour indefinitely, and the next upgrade finds the same problem plus one more
Rewriting data to satisfy the read without comparing values before and after
verification: Value-by-value comparison over the declared business key when the fix touched data. When the fix was a configuration, the output of the same query on both runtimes has to match
rollback: Remove the configuration, or restore the data from before the rewrite. The second is a data rollback and needs the consumers inventoried first
